I don’t think it is because it seems to me she was an attractive homeless girl and she deserved some of my money.

Do you believe that as well? Not so su- not so convinced.

C’mon Karl. Don’t worry about him. He doesn’t kn- he doesn’t understand radio, Karl. He-he-he-he- I heard his show before he had us. He was doing it. He sounded just like Dr. Fox.

“My family was killed, but look! A Carpet Warehouse!”

That Steve read the papers more often

That-that was one of- I just had to listen to them. They just kept stopping me in the street as I was trying to get to the tube. “You’ve got to stop ‘Rockbusters.’ It’s run out of steam,” they said and I’m glad.

They make their way to Leicester Square for three o’ clock.

Switch off the phone or very least, get out.

f: Steve: "HE GAVE YOU A PET!" Ricky later revealed the cat was named Ollie, not Jonathan.
ex: Jonathan Ross, gave you, a cat! As a replacement for your cat which died! Now to me, that’s an inappropriate gift!
That’s – You should be – I don’t think people should be giving PETS, as gifts – imagine –

q: Watching a documentary about Nazi Germany, Steve admitted to a guilty feeling. What was it?
a: Feeling smug that he'd have been okay, being tall and blonde
x: He found Hitler's speeches quite gripping
He reckoned he'd have made a brilliant spy
He fancied himself as a U-boat captain
f: Steve: "I'm slightly smug that I know I'd have been okay because I'm tall and blonde, almost blue eyed."
ex: I was watching a documentary about Nazi Germany, everything and I realized that I felt guilty for quite a while because whenever I see a program about the Nazi plan, I always take a certain solace. Like I'm slightly smug that I know I'd…
And that's what they were after, wasn't it? The sort of Superman. The Aryan.
Well, Steve would have been the Aryan pin up.
Yeah, I'm like a kind of poster boy. Nazi Arabs.

q: Karl wanted "Do to others as you'd like to be treated yourself" popped through people's doors. What did Steve say Karl's whole government seemed to rely on?
x: Putting up posters in the chippy
Asking the neighbours to sort it out
f: Steve: "maybe sometimes you've got to instigate something to be a little bit more strong-minded than f***ing leaflets, my friend."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Society · 2009
ex: I like that saying-- The one about "Do to others as you'd like to be treated yourself."
That's a good one. Pop that on a leaflet. Pop it through the door.

But you seem to be doing a lot of leafleting. That seems to be-- your entire governance seems to be guided by popping leaflets through doors. And I get a lot of leaflets, so I'm presuming the rest of the country does, and it's not always…

q: Steve asked if Karl was worried crickets aren't aware of the dangers of wasps. What did he ask if Karl had done "amongst the cricket community"?
f: Sarcasm aside, Karl had only looked it up online: "oh, it's a popular thing that happens."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Society · 2009
ex: So, you were worried that crickets aren't aware of the dangers of wasps? You did a bit of leafleting amongst the cricket community?

I just had a look online and saw that, oh, it's a popular thing that happens. It's like a bit of a mugging. It said you can leave them for about half an hour, they normally come round and they don't know they've had an egg put in their…

q: Steve imagined the circus hippo fretting that the trampoline act had upstaged it. What was the hippo's own act, according to Steve?
f: "He's already done the trampoline! My pogo stick act is never gonna work!"
ex: He’s going “How can I follow this? How can I – this is really annoying. They’re gonna be – ohhh no.”
He’s thinking “He’s already done the trampoline! My pogo stick act is never gonna work!”

q: Steve reckoned Karl had got dimmer since they came back on air. What did he say it was like?
a: BSE (mad cow disease) had kicked in
x: He'd been hit on the head by a coconut
f: Steve: "It's like BSE has kicked in." Then he decided they'd just forgotten: "he forgets we're on the radio. There's just dead air."
ex: Why is it, your brain - It seems like since we've come back on air you have become dimmer, I mean, it is extraordinary. It's like-it's like BSE (Mad Cow Disease) has kicked in and you really are..
Or - did we just forget, we just forgot-
Maybe it's just been a long time. We forgot just how stupid he is, it’s proper, it's the silences- he forgets we’re on the radio. There's just dead air.

q: Steve insisted DJing isn't just about the songs you play, it's the way you play them. Which detail did he call 'very important'?
x: How loud you have the bass
Whether you wave your arms about
f: Ricky helpfully added the other key skill: "Leave your hand on them... as they try and go round."
ex: You can tell he hasn't been a DJ, because it's not just about...
It's not just about the songs you play, it's the way you play them.
The way you play them...whether it's 33 or 45, very important.
Yeah! Yeah! Leave your hand on them...

q: Steve imagined doing his own version of Fatboy Slim's huge Brighton beach gig. Where would it be, and with whom?
f: Fatboy Slim had 20,000 people on Brighton beach. Ricky reckoned Steve's crowd would be "86 people."
ex: 'I don't know what I was thinking', but I like the idea, cos you know Fat Boy Slim did Brighton beach, didn't he and he had like 20,000 people in Brighton beach.
Everyone was loving it, just the idea of me down in Weston-super-Mare, doing the same...
...with 86 people. Have you ever seen that thing Karaoke Challenge, on Challenge TV?

q: A friend's girlfriend saw Steve on Channel 4's 'Top Ten TV Bastards'. What backhanded compliment did she pay him?
a: He's better looking on TV than in real life
x: He's shorter on TV than in real life
He's funnier on TV than in real life
He looks less like a lamppost on TV
f: Steve: "I'm not on TV, so it's not beneficial in any way." Ricky: "sooner or later you have to step out of the TV."
ex: Whoa, whoa, whoa, stop there though Rick, cos I was on TV briefly, there was a thing about The Office on Top Ten TV Bastards on Channel 4 and I appeared on there briefly talking about the show, and, erm, there's this girl who's girlfriend…
... well I'm not on TV, so it's not beneficial in any way.
Yeah and sooner or later you have to step out of the TV.
But that's like saying, I normally find you pretty repulsive, my opinion changed slightly last night cos you were on the box, but it didn't, it sounded like a compliment.
Through the aid of a different...
Through the aid of lighting, and appearing for 12 seconds on screen, in small doses...

q: Steve shared a worry about aliens ever visiting Earth. What is it?
a: They'll bump into Karl and think he represents mankind
x: They'll pick up XFM and think it's all we've got
They'll take Ricky back to their planet
f: Karl's reaction to the idea of an alien visit: "I'd love that!" Steve: "What if they bump into you and they think you represent mankind."
ex: Rick what worries mee-ee-what worries me is if one day aliens do visit--
(high pitched, amazed) "I'd love that! I'd love-"
--worries me is they might bump into you-WHAT if they bump into you!? What if they bump into you and they think you represent mankind.

q: For school Comic Relief day, Steve dressed as a clown with a red nose, a wig and a big bow tie his mum made. What was on his feet?
f: "The shoes, obviously. I just wore my regular shoes." Only three people in the whole school dressed up. Ricky: "But Steve, you're 50p up!"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Comic Relief · 2011
ex: The shoes, obviously. I just wore my regular shoes.
But I had the red nose, a wig.

You know, the whole deal. Big bow tie that my mum made for me. I thought, this is going be to the best day ever. Right, get to school. I want you to picture this scene right, during the assembly in my class of 30. School uniform. School…

q: Steve shared one of his favourite quotations, from an American novelist whose name he'd forgotten. What did it say fame is?
a: A mask that eats into the face
x: A coat that never quite fits
A drug with a nasty comedown
A mirror that only shows the front
f: For once Karl approved: "Yeah that's alright, yeah... I like that."
ex: One of my favourites is, from an American novelist and the quote is, talking about the subject of fame and being famous: "fame is a mask that eats into the face", don't you think that’s amazing?

Well, meaning that the fame, that fame is something that is artificial, that you wear initially when you become famous, but it’s ethereal, it’s nothing, it’s intangible, it’s just an artifice, but if you stay famous long enough, you begin…
It was an American novelist... I forget his name
Yeah that’s alright, yeah... I like that

q: As Ricky "played with fire" by choosing an eight-minute song, Steve warned he could scald his hands. What else did Steve say was at risk?
f: Steve instantly regretted it: "I wish I knew what that meant... I didn't really think that through."
ex: You think I'm playing with fire?
Ohhh Careful, Rick, careful. Because you could scold your hands, but what about your elbows?
I wish I knew what that meant. I wish I knew what that meant. I didn't really think that through...

q: During a bomb scare, Steve and his friends warned a pub landlord about a suspicious bag in the street. What did the landlord do with it?
a: Put a sandwich board over it
x: Threw a bucket of water over it
Stuck a traffic cone on it
f: It was the board advertising the pub's food. Steve: "That is fail-safe..." Ricky: that's what the bomb disposal unit use, "very often".
ex: Livid, there was one time right, I was down in the centre of town, this was after some of the big explosions, the IRA had, you know, and various things and everyone was on bomb alert, very nervous, very scared, and there was a sort of, a…
That is what the bomb disposal unit use, very often, you'll see them up and down Oxford Street, they're not people selling, you know, selling stuff, that's a bomb shield...

They'll leave it on a bomb... I love the idea, cos what we did we moved about 100 yards down the road, cos we thought if the bomb goes off we want to see it that would be dramatic, but we don't wanna get injured.

q: Steve put the return of Rockbusters to a listener vote. Why did he say it had to be by email only?
a: "We don't want to speak to these freaks"
f: Ricky loved that: "I love the fact we don't want to speak these freaks, we work with one of them!"
ex: No let’s e-mail only we don’t want to speak to these freaks.
I love the fact we don’t want to speak these freaks, we work with one of them! God.

q: Picturing the Antarctic scientists getting Ricky's message, Steve imagined one of them complaining that they'd actually voted for whom?
f: Ricky had imagined a slightly underwhelmed reaction: "Eh, fella from The Office", "Oh yeah. Go on".
ex: "Eh, fella from The Office', 'Oh yeah. Go on'. I mean-
-so I don't know I can enhance-I mean I get compared to-
One of them's going 'I voted for Ricky Martin! What?'

q: Steve reckoned the four-hour queues to see the late Pope could have been done in about three-quarters of an hour. How?
a: Wheel him past everyone on a dessert trolley
x: Put him on an airport travelator
Show him on a big screen in the square
Drive him round in an open-top bus
f: Steve despaired: "once again people not thinking - they're not expanding their minds." Ricky suggested a rag-week bed down Oxford Street.
ex: You know all that coverage of the Pope with like millions of people that have gathered in Rome and stuff. I was thinking about, remember we talked about the Queen Mother, and they were queuing up and queueing up and queueing up to see the…
Yeah. Like four hours to get a glimpse.
And once again I couldn't help but feel if they popped on some kind of like dessert trolley and just wheeled him past everyone else. They could have gone and done it about three-quarters of an hour.
You know, once again people not thinking - they're not expanding their minds.
Tell you what happened to me...
What like students on rag week with the bed down Oxford street.

q: With no big movie to give away, which VHS did Steve find while moving house and offer as a Rockbusters prize?
f: Ricky guessed "Burt Reynolds?" but it starred Kurt Russell, "with Steven Seagal in a, uh, cameo as well."
ex: …’cause I noticed there’s not a big movie this week and we normally give away a big movie. I was moving house this week and I found a video that you’re more than welcome to if you’re a fan. Uhm…
No, it stars Kurt Russell… “Executive Decision”!
I’ve got that to give away if you’re interested, “Executive Decision” with Steven Seagal in a, uh, cameo as well, so uh…
…I think it’s on, I think it’s on TV this week, Rick, so if you miss it this coming Friday…

q: Karl wondered if a celebrity could slim by purposely having about eight tapeworms. What did Steve call this diet plan?
f: Ricky worked out the method: "let them eat your meal and then take them out."
ex: Well I was thinking that. Could- you know. I mean you’re a fan of Waller. Could he purposely have about eight of them?
Cuz they were saying how they eat, a lot of stuff when they’re in you. They just eat...

Well, they take enough so you don’t die and nor do they, yeah. I mean you’ve got to keep taking them out, haven’t ya. Cuz you’ll still have the same weight, cuz it’s gotta go somewhere. So you’ll have them in ya. What you’ve got to do is…
Do you think WormWatchers will catch on?

q: As Steve's TV delivery man left, he held his hand out expecting a tip. What had Steve actually reached into his pocket for?
a: His mobile phone, which was ringing
f: Steve: "I went, 'It's just my phone.'" He didn't chase him with a fiver either: "I'm not made of money. I just spent it all on a TV."
ex: But the problem was I didn't realize and I was thinking to myself, "I wonder if I've got tip him?" And the guy was leaving, and my mobile phone went off in my pocket.
And I reach in to get it, he put his hand out thinking it was a tip. I went, I went, "It's just my phone."
Then so, I felt terrible after he left. I didn't know, I what, what was I gonna do run down the street and offer him a fiver.
Of course not, I'm not made of money. I just spent it all on a TV.

q: Steve said that when he uses a word Karl doesn't understand, like "arbitrary", Karl's face reminds him of what?
x: A fruit machine stuck on lemons
f: Ricky: "You lost him on 'Arbitrary'." Steve said Karl's face "just goes dead", and Ricky wondered what Karl's version of control-alt-delete would be.
ex: Last week after your nervous breakdown. You went to Hastings. Can I ask why the hell did you go to Hastings? It's so arbitrary.
You lost him on "Arbitrary". Why did you choose that above all other places within...?
It's amazing, isn't it? You look at his face when you say a word, you know, he does understand and it just goes dead.
It's like when a your computer freezes.

Yeah. It is like it is like that, yeah. Is there is there an equivalent to control-alt-delete when karl just doesn't understand something you have to press... like knob, bollock, finger up arse. It takes him out of his sort of stupid…

q: Which question from Steve finally made Karl give up on his reverse-ageing population plan?
a: Aren't the family getting younger too?
x: Who's paying for all the injections?
Do they have to give their pension back?
f: Karl: "Forget it then. We'll leave it as it is." Steve was relieved to hear no more "from the diaries of Charles Manson."
ex: And then what happens? So when does it die? When it gets to naught. When it's one. When it's nought days old, it goes through-
Yeah, it just dies. People know. It's almost like a countdown. See, the family's aware of it.
But aren't the family getting younger? What's happened to the family? I mean I don't-
Forget it then. We'll leave it as it is.
Leave it as it is. Shall we?
Shall we? Can we all agree on that, guys? Now should we agree to leave it as it is? Is that alright? 'Cause I don't want to hear any more from the diaries of Charles Manson.

q: Karl wanted to redesign the intestine as a straight tube with filters along the way. What kind of intestine did Steve say he was dreaming up?
f: Ricky explained that the length increases the surface area for absorption. Steve: "I don't think you're gonna improve on it."
ex: Just-just have a, just have a straight, do you know what I mean, straight down--
It's to increase the surface area for absorption. So, a foot long intestine, you wouldn't absorb much food. Whereas, you go down, you know.
Yeah but just have more points in it where it has to go through some sort of filter.
What are you talking about? Again...the evolution sort of worked this out for us. It really works.
I don't think you're gonna improve on it. In your mind you-some kind of what, some kind of kerplunk style intestine--

q: Under Karl's chopped-up queue plan, what did Steve say he'd be annoyed to find after queuing 12 hours to see the head?
f: Steve: "I can understand those that queued for 12 hours to see the head, I'd be a little bit annoyed if I got there to find a toe!"
ex: No, just a very quick question, I can understand those that queued for 12 hours to see the head, i'd be a little bit annoyed if I got there to find a toe!

q: What did Steve suggest Ricky's would-be escapee salamander had its eye on?
a: The DVD player, so it could flog it down the market
f: Steve, as the salamander: "I can have it and be down the market." Karl's only question was: "Are they dangerous?"
ex: But what’s the worst that could happen, Karl?
What’s it thinking? What do you think it is thinking this salamander?
It’s got its eye on the DVD player?
I can have it and be down the market.

q: Steve described a group of Japanese tourists approaching Ricky in the street. What did they actually want?
a: For Ricky to take a photo of them
x: A photo with Ricky from 'The Office'
f: They didn't recognise him. Steve imagined them back home: "Taken WITH Ricky Gervais?" "No, taken BY Ricky Gervais."
ex: They-they appeared behind a corner and I thought, “This is odd. They-” you know, they seemed like tourists, but they’re obviously going to ask for an autograph. And they just handed him a camera and said, “Excuse me, would you take a photo…
I was, I was cracking up.
And they didn’t recognize him. They didn’t recognize him.
I was laughing. I was thinking, “Right.” Oh, dear.
So now Ricky’s stood in the street. People are recognizing him as he’s taking a photo of three complete Japanese strangers.
And I imagine them getting home and sort of saying, “And here’s the one we had taken by Ricky Gervais.” “Taken with Ricky Gervais?” “No, taken by Ricky Gervais.”

q: Steve said he wasn't accusing Ricky of being lazy, but pointed out what about how he was sitting?
a: He was sat on a chair yet almost vertical
x: He was lying on the studio floor
He'd fallen asleep with his headphones on
He was sitting on the desk with his feet up
f: "You're sat on a chair and yet you're almost vertical." Ricky predicted he'd be "bent double" in old age.
ex: But to be fair, Rick, I’m not, I’m not accusing you of being lazy--
But you’re sat on a chair and yet you’re almost vertical.
I don’t know how’ve you done it. It’s like you’re almost asleep, but you’re sat on that right chair. I don’t know how you’ve- you angled yourself in that way!
I’m gonna have a bad back when I’m- ohh. In old age. I’m just going to be bent double.

q: Hearing that baby Karl just lay there looking worried and stressed, Steve said it sounded like which horror film?
f: Steve: "It sounds like that horror film... It sounds like 'Pilkinton's Baby'. Just you lying there in your cot."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The English · 2009
ex: Always had a bit of a worried look on my face. Didn't say much, just always listened. My eyes moved about more than I did. Sat there looking around. Looking stressed.
(laughs) "Me eyes moved about more than I did!" Oh dear! Couldn't walk.
"Well, I can't walk but I'm trying to get a bit of movement in my face." It's a workout. A baby workout. Alright babies! Well, if you can't walk, what about your face? Let your face do the walking.
It sounds like that horror film... It sounds like 'Pilkinton's Baby'.
Just you lying there in your cot.

q: Steve's grandfather had all his teeth pulled out while in the RAF during the war. What were they replaced with?
a: A wooden plate with fake teeth attached
x: A set made from old Spitfire parts
A gold plate he won at cards
f: He's never had it changed, so it's still the wooden plate "but about three teeth still hanging on it".
ex: ...he was in the RAF, in the war, right, and he, for some reason he had problems with his teeth and they pulled them all out...

...and they replaced them with, erm, with, er, a false set of false teeth, but during the war time, I don't know whether this was just, like, what it was like during the war, or just the '40s, but he had a kind of wooden plate put in with…
...erm, and he's never had that changed. So, now, he's still got the wooden plate but about three teeth still hanging on it...

q: At the cinema, a trailer explained the boy in Spielberg's AI is really a robot. What did a woman near Steve ask her husband?
x: "Is this the film we came for?"
"Is that the lad from Home Alone?"
f: Steve: "So already... my back's up." Then, when the title Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon came up, she said: "Funny name for a film!"
ex: And, um, so they've arbitrarily chosen this film. So she's in there, the trailers come on. And it's not only is she greedy, but you can tell she's stupid. This trailer comes on for AI, remember that film, Spielberg film, AI?
And um, and that, the trailer is something like, uh, "Jimmy is a 12-year-old boy.

He doesn't, he feels like a human. He da da da. He experiences emotion like a human. But he's not a human. He's a *robot.* Right. And everyone goes quiet. And she went to her husband, "How old was he again?"
So already, I'm, I'm f- ugh - my back's up, you know what I mean?

q: Inspired by a trailer for 'The Farmer Wants a Wife', what TV show did Steve pitch on air?
f: He was happy to let the public vote: "I'll have anything, whatever they can choose." Then an even better idea: "Steve Merchant wants a farmer!"
ex: And I'm thinking "Hello, idea, Steve Merchant Wants a Wife".
Who sounds a bit like a farmer.
Exactly, what I'm saying is, I don't mind the public voting for the woman, if that's how it happens, 'cos, you know, who cares? I'll have anything, whatever they can choose, fine, you know.
Steve Merchant wants a farmer! Even better.

q: Steve claimed he turned down 'a woman on a plate' while walking home from the shops on a Friday night. How was the 50-something woman dressed?
a: In a rhinestone cowboy type outfit
x: In a wedding dress and veil
f: Ricky's first thought: "Parton? Was it Parton". Steve confirmed: "It wasn't Dolly."
ex: Yeah, I was just thinking, with Karl, he likes to have a little dig every so often about, you know, err, my success with the ladies, but I tell you, you'd have been proud of me last night, no listen, you'd have been proud of me. I was…
And there was this woman coming the other way who must have been 50, 55, staggering down the street, dressed in kind of rhinestone cowboy type outfit, really weird, never seen her before.

It wasn't Dolly, and she was staggering down the road, just "argh" just shouting, and this truck drove by, and she just went "Oyy! Come over here, come over here", and the car just drove by, whatever, and she walks over to me, and she saw…

q: Steve legged it from the staggering woman who blocked his path. He said the encounter was like a nightmare from which fairy tale?
f: Ricky took it further: inside there are "loads of other people that look just like you" and "they're getting very very thin."
ex: I'm in a mood to make whoopee, but, I thought it's probably best to avoid it, and I actually managed to run away, and avoid her, and she kept shouting at me as I was running down the road, "come with me, come with me", but I legged it.…
Yeah, you go in there, and there's loads of other people that look just like you.
And they're getting very very thin.

q: Steve told a man going through his bins to take what he wanted. What did Steve catch him doing the next day?
a: Selling Steve's junk at a pavement stall outside the 7-11
x: Wearing Steve's old clothes outside his house
Dumping it all back in Steve's front garden
f: He'd even marked prices on everything. Steve spotted a Yellow Pages and bought it back: "50p, I snapped it up."
ex: Yeah, going through everything. He'd torn the bags open, he was going through it. I said to him, "What you up to?" He went, "Oh yeah, just looking… stuff. Don't worry I just- I'll clean it all up afterwards just looking for a few odds and…
How much was the yellow pages?
I thought that was a bargain. And um- it was incredible he had- the cheek of just selling our junk outside.

q: Ricky said he likes to squeeze little bald heads like an egg. What did Steve worry would happen if Karl's head ever actually cracked?
x: It would turn out to be hollow
There'd be a smaller head inside
f: Steve: "if you ever actually did crack Karl's head, I think yolk would come out." Ricky: "Yeah, I know!"
ex: Yeah! Yeah. Aw, I lo- cause he’s got his little round head, I’ve got another mate who’s got a little bald head and I like to squeeze it.
To see how far- d’you know what I mean? Like an egg. It- you can squeeze it that way, sort of sideways and that hurts, but then squeeze it forward to back; it doesn’t hurt so much, does it?
Do you know what worries me is I think if you ever actually did crack Karl’s head, I think yolk would come out.
(giggling) Yeah, I know! I do- he was forward, drawing, and I gave him a little karate chop on the back of the head and he jumped! He spasmed!

q: As Steve set off excitedly for his first game of cricket, what did his mum tell him?
a: A cricket ball once hit her on the head and knocked her out for two hours
x: She'd broken her nose trying to catch a cricket ball
A cricket ball once smashed through her kitchen window
She'd seen a lad lose his front teeth to a cricket bat
f: Before his first rugby game she did it again: "be careful with rugby. I knew a kid once, broke his back playing it."
ex: Well, it's weird you say it because I remember the, the first day I went to play cricket, my mum said as I was leaving I was really excited about playing cricket. She went, be careful. I was walking across a playing field once, a cricket…
I was terrified of it. Such a scary game.

q: What did Steve call an 'utter waste of time'?
a: Buying a fake Rolex and then telling people it's fake
x: Buying a real Rolex and keeping it in a drawer
Wearing a watch when you've got a mobile
Getting a Rolex engraved with your own name
f: Steve mocked the thinking behind it: "I'm getting one over on the Rolex people!"
ex: I know what it was, it was about, you said about the, erm, about the sort of, the fire and that, that idea of kind of buying a-. It's like when people buy a fake Rolex watch...
...and they tell people it's fake. Utter waste of time.
Why have you told me that? It's like, what, you're not, you're, "I'm getting one over on the Rolex people!"

q: Steve enjoyed Ten Benson's 'Black Snow' but worried they were teenagers trying to sound like they'd had a hard life. Which band did he say does that?
f: Claire reassured him they're not teenagers, but "they're dirty." Steve: "Good good."
ex: I love it. It’s sort punk but it’s got more in common with stuff like Steppenwolf and Bad Company.
My only worry is that erm, are they like eighteen year olds who, like Gomez, are trying to sound like they’ve kind of had a rough hard living life?
Well no no they’re not they sort of but they’re, they’re dirty.

q: According to Steve, what's the definitive track to get a wedding disco going again after the buffet and the speeches?
a: Oh What a Night by Frankie Valli and the Four Seasons
x: Hi Ho Silver Lining by Jeff Beck
f: Steve says it leads "straight into a '70s medley" and claims guests told him "You're amazing I don't know how you do it".
ex: Can I tell you what the definitive track is?
Oh What a Night, Frankie Valli and The Four Seasons. Do do do, people don't realise what it is exactly, straight away. Do Do do, baum daun ba daun, I can't actually play it, but err.

"Oh what a night" click click click "Late December back in sixty" That leads you straight into a ‘70s medley, and everyone's lovin' that, I'm thinking Bee Gees, there's gonna probably be some kind of Abba track, Dancing Queen would go down…

q: Steve insisted his battered new hat made him look a bit like Tom Waits or who?
f: Steve: "I think this genuinely looks good." Ricky taped it on a camcorder to put up on rickygervais.com.
ex: Right. Um, can I take a picture of this, and I'll put it on my website? Right. I am now taping this on a camcorder. I will put this up on rickygervais.com.

I disagree. I think this genuinely looks good. I think it makes me look a bit like, say Tom Waits, or um, Farmer Barleymow. The point is this, right? I'm wearing the hat; I'm looking good, okay? But people, obviously, they can sense that…

q: Where did Steve hide his two million Vietnamese dong so muggers wouldn't find it?
a: In a money belt under his T-shirt
f: If mugged, Steve could just say "I haven't got any money on me". Karl's verdict: "But that's still out of reach, innit?"
ex: I don't have a bum bag. I have a, I have a um, I have a money belt that I wear underneath the t-shirt-
So as not to see, y'know, so people don't think I've got any money on me.
And if I get mugged I can just go, "I haven't got any money on me". Because they would never think to look-
-underneath the shirt and see the money belt.
But that's still out of reach, innit? Over there?

q: At a market in Vietnam, the whole crowd ended up laughing at Steve. What did a woman attach to his back?
f: A man Steve took for a postman did "a lumbering sort of Frankenstein walk", and old ladies came up to compare their heights.
ex: They started openly pointing and laughing. One of them, right, started. Like I think he was a postman. He looked like, he might be a Vietnamese Postman. I don't know why that should make any difference, but he started doing a sort of…

q: Engineers took about 25 minutes to come and fix XFM's broken desk. What was Steve's theory about why?
a: They fixed Capital, Capital Gold and people's car radios first
x: They were all on a tea break in the canteen
They couldn't find XFM's studio in the building
They'd heard Karl had broken it on purpose
f: Steve: "Do you feel like we're maybe quite low in the pecking order in the building?" Ricky: "Definitely."
ex: You noticed how it took, um-
-about 25 minutes for them to come down as well though. Do you feel like we're maybe quite low in the pecking order in the building?
You know it's like Capital first, Capital gold, they can shoot off, do other sort of pirate stations.
Peoples car radios, then they come back here.

q: In Steve's university story, what was the cleaning lady doing in his room when he came back?
a: Clomping round in his Dr. Martens doing an impression of him
x: Reading his diary to the whole corridor
Using his shoes as plant pots
f: Steve has size 14 feet. Ricky: "I love the fact that she's more popular than you."
ex: And erm, so I was working hard to try and seem kind of cool and not freakish and erm, I came back from studies once and I came in and there's a little old cleaning lady that kind of would always come in every day and clean up our Halls of…
That that's my door's open and I'm not. But I'm not in there and there's people staring in the door and I looked in and the little cleaning lady had my Dr. Martens on and was clomping around.
Making them all laugh, doing an impression of me.
Imagine that! Imagine the psychological scars that has.
I love the fact that she's more popular than you.

q: When Ricky took Steve bowling in Finsbury Park, what did Steve's size 14 bowling shoes look like to Ricky?
f: Ricky: "they're so long and thin... it looked like Krusty's ... Krusty the Clown's feet." Steve: "It is a huge size ... shoe."
ex: So you must have looked like a wall bracket with that. What is that? I went bowling with him once the first time and he and we went bowling in this place. Where was it? Must of been Finsbury Park and, uh, I'd never been before and it is…
Anyway and they're multicolored aren't they? They're two colors and it looked like Krusty's ... Krusty the Clown's feet. And then that it's Steve's going "alright." 14, that is big innit?
It is a huge size ... shoe. You're right.

q: Karl reckoned his aunt wouldn't read Zoo magazine, so he'd got away with it. What was Steve's quip?
a: She's more of a Nuts woman
x: She only reads the Racing Post
She's more of a People's Friend woman
She gets all her news from Teletext
f: Karl's plan backfired anyway: a cousin read the article and phoned his mam, who told him, "I wish you wouldn't, you know, talk about Aunty Nora."
ex: And uhh, anyway, so this was in there, right, and I was saying in the magazine, you know, but I think I got away with it. She doesn't doesn't listen to the show, but you know, I don't think she reads Zoo magazine, so..
She's more of a Nuts woman.

q: What did a couple of sixth-formers shout at Steve on Finchley Road?
f: Steve asked boxer Ricky to pop round and have a word. Ricky: "an enemy of yours is an enemy of mine."
ex: It's just- I was walking down Finchley Road the other day and a couple of sixth-formers said, "Oy, yah lanky goggle-eyed freak" and I just wondered if maybe you could pop 'round and have a word with them?
Yeah... an enemy of yours is an enemy of mine.

q: Steve bought himself a 'treat': the classic London tourist postcard of a woman's breasts with what painted on them?
f: Steve: the best way to remember London "is...a picture...of a woman's breasts...with....pictures of CATS, painted on them". Ricky: "They are the most grotesque things."
ex: Uh Dickens, "Yeah I've seen um, Big Ben, I've seen The House of Parliament, I've seen the wonderful things. The best way for me to remember that...is...a picture...of a woman's breasts"--
--"with....pictures of CATS, painted on them". I've brought them in.
They are the most grotesque things.

q: Steve's grandparents put the roast on at 7am to eat it at 6pm. What phrase do they use for a really good meal?
a: "That's lovely. You could suck it away"
f: Steve: "Who wants that from a roast dinner? You may as well blend it up and serve it as a broth."
ex: So the problem is that they have to get up. They get up at 7:00 in the morning to put on say, you know, some beef or lamb whichever they're going to cook. They put it on at 6:00 in the morning, 7:00 in the morning, so that by the time they…
You could suck it away. Who wants that from a roast dinner? You may as well blend it up--
And serve it as a broth.
I don't want that phrase coming from old people without teeth.

q: Steve got so riled up at Ricky's fight that he went crazy. What did he start shouting to try to freak everyone out?
a: "Kiss him! Snog him, lick him! Ask him out!"
f: After starting with "Smash his face!", Steve changed tactics "in a vain attempt to throw someone."
ex: I mean I've never been to a fight before, and I just was like, "Come onnn!" I was like, "Smash his face!" I was really shouting it, I was just going crazy!
Shouting for me though, were ya?
No I'm shouting for y- and then I was-
Then I just decided to try and freak everyone- so I was shouting, "Kiss him! Snog him, lick him! Ask- ask him out!"
I was shouting that in a vain attempt to throw someone.

q: Steve offered an answer to Karl's hat puzzle that Karl rejected but said he liked "a lot". What was it?
f: Karl: "Aw, that's a good one though." Ricky added the man had fallen on the moon, "not that the moon happened, it was... set up."
ex: No. Aw, that's a good one though.
I like that one a lot.
--it works. He's fallen on the moon and they're... uh, not that the moon happened, it was... set up, wasn't it--

q: Steve blurted out "Water" to Karl's fat-free food question. When Ricky threw this back at him, what was Steve's excuse?
a: He thought they weren't taking Karl's question seriously
x: Ricky had peeked at Karl's screen
f: Steve: "BUT THAT'S BECAUSE I THOUGHT WE WEREN'T TAKIN' THE QUESTION SERIOUSLY". Ricky wasn't having it: "YOU SAID WATER! YOU SAID WATER!"
ex: Because you’re supposed to write it down!
But you didn’t – I – what do you mean I didn’t know?! You’re supposed to write it down, that’s the whole point, we’re writing things down!
YOU SAID WATER! YOU SAID WATER!
BUT THAT’S BECAUSE I THOUGHT WE WEREN’T TAKIN’ THE QUESTION SERIOUSLY, ‘CAUSE HE DIDN’T KNOW WHAT HE’S TALKIN’ ABOUT!
We’ve got to set the rules, this is ludicrous!

q: Introducing an "old school" track for his hip hop feature, Steve was asked how he spells "school". His answer?
f: Steve: "Going back in time, rewinding the past." The track was by Digital Underground, the group Steve said featured Tupac Shakur when he first began.
ex: I’m playing an old school track this week, Rick.
Going back in time, rewinding the past.

q: Steve revealed Jonathan Ross had phoned Ricky for advice on clothes. Which look did Steve say Ricky was "goin' for"?
a: The man down the DSS look
f: Steve also asked whether Ricky had "a single pair of trousers that aren't elasticated at the waist." Ross: "I like that look".
ex: I love the fact, you were on the phone to Gervais last night, weren’t you, asking his advice,
He’s goin’ for the man down the DSS look!
I like that look – no, it’s a nice look!
Have you got a single pair of trousers that aren’t elasticated at the waist.

q: Caller Neil told them The Office was "a shoo-in" at the Comedy Awards. What did Steve admit?
a: He didn't know what a shoo-in is, but he'd like to go to one
x: He'd rather it was a shoo-out
f: Ricky's translation: "I think he means like, erm, foot in the door." Neil: "no, not foot in the door".
ex: Oh you guys are a shoo-in.
You - you're a shoo-in. It's yours.
Thank you. I don't know what a shoo-in is, but I'd like to go to one.
I think he means like, erm, foot in the door.
Yeah - no, not foot in the door -

q: Ricky and Steve discussed instruments that aren't right for war. Which one did Steve say was 'a bit too carnival'?
f: Ricky agreed: "Maracas. Yeah. Too happy." He also put forward the grand piano, which Steve said "wouldn't be appropriate at all".
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to The World Cup · 2010
ex: Because there's certain instruments that aren't appropriate for war. Like maracas.
It's just a bit too carnival.
That wouldn't be appropriate at all.

q: Steve said Karl was imagining the ageing girl's life like which music video?
a: The Fat Boy Slim one where something crawls out of the sea and evolves
x: The Michael Jackson one where faces morph into each other
The Peter Gabriel one with stop-motion dancing fruit
The Radiohead one where a man lies down on the pavement
f: Steve set Karl straight: "She's not living a life, a whole life, in like, you know, three weeks."
ex: I think you’re thinking of her life like that Fat Boy Slim video where it starts off as something crawling out of the sea and then it evolves really quickly over three minutes. I mean, that’s not the case, Karl. Her mind isn’t- she isn’t…
She’s not living a life, a whole life, in like, you know, three weeks. It’s just her body is-is degenerating quicker than it should.

q: Spotting Dr. Fox at number 39 on the radio "Power List", what did Steve joke had helped him up it?
f: Ricky agreed: "that sneaks him up the list, yeah." Ricky himself was 56th.
ex: Just checking to see, uh- oh, yeah, Dr. Fox. Good, he’s on there at number thirty-nine. I’m assuming his medical qualifications have also pitched in in the--
Yeah, that’s the- yeah, that sneaks him up the list, yeah.

q: After Steve read out emails saying Rockbusters had run its course, what did Karl predict Steve would come in with next week?
a: Another hip hop track full of effin' and jeffin'
x: A quiz about the Star Wars films
A phone-in about tall people's problems
f: Karl's comeback to the bad reviews: "Alright, well we'll see what you come up with next week... At five to one."
ex: Alright, well we’ll see what you come up with next week. Let’s see what you do, see what you come in with.
I’m guessing you’ll be popping in with another hip hop track--

q: When Karl explained what he thought Freud's message was, Steve joked that Freud had also come up with which advertising slogan?
a: Go to work on an egg
x: A Mars a day helps you work, rest and play
Have a break, have a KitKat
f: Steve, deadpan: "He also came up with Go to work on an egg." Ricky: "Oh, Christ Almighty."
ex: He's just saying, drink milk all your life. It's good for you.
No, he's not saying drink milk all your life. What is this? Is this an advert he's doing?
He also came up with Go to work on an egg.

q: Steve brought in 'a little gag' he'd heard 'from some fella' the night before. Why are London buses red?
a: You'd be red if you had to come every ten minutes
x: They've been stuck in traffic all day
They've been out in the sun too long
f: Steve called it "a simple little joke". Ricky was diplomatic: "It's great."
ex: Heard it last night from some fella. Why are London buses red?
You'd be red if you had to come every ten minutes. What do you think?

q: Steve unveiled his 'perfect murder' on XFM. What was the murder weapon?
a: An arrow made of ice, fired from a bow
x: An icicle dropped from a rooftop
A poisoned snowball thrown through a window
A frozen dart fired from a blowpipe
f: Fire it through the victim's window and it melts: "Murder weapon? It's gone. Gone into the thin air. The wet patch dries."
ex: It's so simple, I don't believe other people ever thought of it. What you do is say you want to murder lives in the street opposite, lives in the house opposite say. What you do is you rent a room opposite theirs, all right? You wait until…
And you get yourself a bow, right, and you fire that ice arrow, okay, across the street, through the window, into the heart of the person you want to murder, right.

They stumble to the ground, and then the ice arrow melts. Gervais, murder weapon? It's gone. Gone into the thin air. The wet patch dries. All right? The police arrive. They can't find the murder weapon. Safe.

q: Playing along with Karl's 'world too heavy' worry, Steve claimed Atlantis proved it. Why did he say Atlantis sank?
a: Its king kept ordering stuff by mail order
x: It kept all its gold in one corner
f: Ricky chipped in that the king bought "Carpets, a lot of carpets" and "all the myrrh, that the wise men didn't want."
ex: Right and what happened is they just kept buying stuff in, mail order. They just kept ordering stuff, like the king and stuff- just kept ordering stuff in mail order. He brought girls across, you know-
Carpets he kept buying, TV se- big screen TV's and stuff like that and eventually-
He bought up all the myrrh, that the wise men didn't want.
Yeah he just- cos he's from like olden times, and he just kept buying stuff, crazy, like he was just a shopaholic basically.
And he was ludicrous, it was li- an- and in the end it was too heavy and it just sunk.

q: When Karl stared blankly at Ricky's question about face transplants, Steve said he looked like someone caught by the police doing what?
a: Holding a mallet over a dead body
x: Climbing out of a bank window
Carrying a telly down the high street
Driving off in a stolen milk float
f: Ricky compared Karl to a cat being asked "Who wants some food, then?": "it's almost like he can understand what we're saying."
ex: It makes sense. But it's not just your face that you lose, but it's the muscle. It's muscle tissue and bones, isn't it, when it's, like, disfigured? Could be through fire or whatever or disease or anything. So they can't just literally…
You're asking Karl like he's gonna know!
Like he- I forgot then. Then he looked at- Was that in Russian?

I wish we could get. I wish we get him on telly just to show the look on his face when I said that. Yeah, it was brilliant, wasn't it? It was. You know when you go to a cat "Who wants some food, then?" he just looks at you, and you go…
It's like if you had been caught holding a mallet over a dead body by the police. Just staring at them blankly.

q: Karl didn't make his point to jellyfish expert Vicky because it might have confused her. Finish Steve's reply: "Well, she's a scientist..."
f: Karl had held back because raising it "would have took her off and confused her".
ex: No, but the turtle thing, you know, if you get rid of 'em then the turtles, you know, won't have anything to eat... But, when she said that, I mean, I couldn't say it cuz it would have took her off and confused her but, like--
Well, she's a scientist, she's easily confused.

q: Jane gave Ricky a golfing break for Christmas, but she doesn't play golf. What did Steve reckon the present really was?
a: An excuse for Jane to have a day off from Ricky
x: A hint that Ricky should lose weight
A way to get Karl out of the office
A bribe to stop Ricky singing at home
f: Steve acted it out: "But you don't play golf, Jane!" "I know, I know! Go!" Ricky added: "A bowling ball with my name on it."
ex: Yeah. It just sounds like an excuse for Jane to have a day off from you!
"But you don't play golf, Jane!" "I know, I know! Go!"
A bowling ball with my name on it.

q: Gary Kemp stopped by while Ricky and Steve were having lunch. Steve then said "don't take this the wrong way" to Ricky. What came next?
a: Gary Kemp had aged better than him
x: Gary Kemp had better hair than him
Gary Kemp was the better singer
Gary Kemp was much taller than him
f: Ricky: "Well, how could I take that the wrong way?" Steve: "It's not offensive... Well he does."
ex: I'll tell you what, we were, me and Steve, were having a little meeting yesterday over lunch about, you know, planning stuff for the show and uh, Gary Kemp came up to me. Started having a little chat about old times and uh, I went "Oh…

Rick, don't take this the wrong way. Remember that sentence "don't take this the wrong way". So there's a right way and a wrong way I could've taken this comment. He went, nodded to sort of Gary Kemp and went "he's aged better than you". I…
No. Well the p-point is this, he- he does possess- he didn't know me, 20 years ago, so he's actually saying: "Rick, don't take this the wrong way. He looks better than you do".

q: Steve doubted 'Rock the Vote' would reach a youth smashing up a bus shelter. Which two stars did he remember being part of it?
f: Steve pictured the yob "throwing bricks at old people" and stopping to say: "What's that? Billy Bragg?"
ex: But it's sort of like, remember that thing when they tried to get young people to vote, do you remember that, was it 'Rock the Vote'?
Was it people like Billy Bragg and people, kind of ...
I just, I don't know who that appeals to, I don't know, y'know, if some youth is kinda smashing up a bus shelter, throwing bricks at old people.
I just can't, I don't believe it ever ... I think it was Mick Hucknall was another one.

q: At a New Year gathering in Bristol, two girls came up to a very tall Steve holding a balloon. What did they want?
a: To use him as a meeting point at midnight
x: To give him a New Year kiss
To invite him back to a party
f: "We're going to meet back at you at midnight." They left in a cab with some lads. Steve: "But then I did have a balloon, so it's a great year for me."
ex: Oh no. I- it was New Year and uh, it- we were all gathering up. You know like in Trafalgar Square at New Year everyone gathers and they have a big kind of party and stuff. Well in Bristol they do something very similar on a smaller scale…
'Are you going to be here for a- for a while?' And I said 'Well, yeah. You know, I probably will.' They said 'It's just that we've arranged to meet back at you. At midnight'.

I was- what do you mean? Cause I was so tall and I had a balloon? I was towering above everyone else. They said- I said- I said- I said 'What?'. They said 'We're going to meet back at you at midnight'.
They said 'Don't worry. You can go about your business because we can see you wherever you are'.

q: At university, Steve found a cashpoint with someone's card still in it and the PIN already entered. What did he press 'just to check'?
a: Balance, to see how much they had
x: Cancel, to give the card back
Change PIN, to teach them a lesson
f: "It was a considerable sum of money... It was not typical student debt." Ricky imagined the options on the screen: "Steal or go to heaven?"
ex: This is like the Marie Celeste. I went to a cash point but I thought “I can’t get my card in here”. So I realised there was already somebody’s card in the machine, they’d put the code in, but, um, but they-they-they-they disappeared…
Um, I pressed ‘Balance’ just to check what their balance was.
It was a considerable sum of money. I’m not going to lie to you. It was not typical student debt. It was, like, I think they were a foreign student, there was a lot of cash in there.

q: Steve was furious to hear he'd missed the free-suit gift lounges before the Emmys. Which star did Ricky say goes round them?
f: Steve fumed: "she's got more money than me. She doesn't need to go and get free stuff." Ricky's explanation: "She's the queen."
ex: Yeah, yeah. The first one I went to, I was mildly embarrassed about. Then I saw like Helen Mirren, the Sopranos.
Bloody Helen Mirren's going around there and I'm not. Yeah, yeah, but she's got more money than me. She doesn't need to go and get free stuff.
She's the queen. She's the richest woman in the world.

q: Ricky spent the 80s running round London and making things out of skip finds. What did Steve say he sounded like?
f: Ricky's reply: "Yeah, but I wasn't shaped like one until I was 32."
ex: So you spent Most of this, the 80s, running around London and collecting debris and making your home outfit. You sound like a womble.
Yeah, but I wasn't shaped like one until I was 32.
And, you know, this is kind of. You were making everything except a living.

q: What reassuring words did Steve's mum offer him on the day of his very first rugby game?
a: That a kid at her school had broken his neck
x: That rugby players all end up toothless
That he'd look silly in the shorts
That he'd probably be picked last
f: Mum: "Enjoy it. Be careful. There was a kid at my school who... broke his neck." Steve: "So I just went to school absolutely petrified."
ex: I never relaxed into rugby because the first day I was going to play it my mum I swear to god my mother said, ‘You’re playing rugby today. You got the kit and everything. Um enjoy it. Be careful. There was a kid at my school who got, um…
Yeah so, thanks very much for that.
So I just went to school absolutely petrified.

q: Karl reminded Steve of all the gig tickets he'd sorted. According to Ricky, which band did Steve get tickets for and then complain it was boring?
f: Ricky also pointed out there were some gigs "he doesn't even turn up to." Karl: "Yeah, we won't even go on about that."
ex: I’ve sorted you out tickets for gigs.
Some he doesn’t even turn up to.
Yeah, we won’t even go on about that. Alright? Lager.
You sorted him out with The Cure, he complained it was boring.

q: Steve finally hit back at Karl's comments about his looks. What did he say Karl looks like?
a: A party balloon with a face drawn on, inflated halfway
x: A boiled egg wearing a parka
A thumb with a face drawn on
A peeled potato in a hat
f: Steve: "You know seriously, can I be honest with you?... Just a little balloon, like a party balloon." Karl's only reply: "Right."
ex: Whenever we get on this conversation, I always think to myself, ‘Karl, do you know what you look like?’

You know seriously, can I be honest with you? You look like- you know if you got like a balloon, a hot air balloon right? Just a little balloon, like a party balloon. If you drew a little face on it, right? And inflated it about halfway…
Ricky laughs and struggles to speak
So. Play a record I don’t wanna get into this. It’s too intense.

q: Steve said Karl had muddled up the story of the mountain piano. Where was it really found, according to Steve?
f: A record-breaker dragged it up as a feat of endurance, then thought "I'll be damned if I'm gonna take it back again" and left it there.
ex: Well, I know for a fact that you've confused. You've confused a few things there because I think the. The piano being found was actually somewhere in Scotland, some kind of moor in Scotland, and they found a piano up there and everyone…
But thought, I'll be damned if I'm gonna take it back again and just left it up there. It wasn't, you know, bloody tipping or aliens or anything.

q: Steve compared the 40 minutes of checks before a flight with our safety checks for donkeys. What were the donkey checks?
a: "Did someone close the gate?" "I think so."
f: Donkeys apparently kill more people than plane crashes, yet "that's our donkey checks." Ricky added: "Is there two holes for the ears?"
ex: But- but my concern is that there's- when you go on a plane there's soo many checks, I mean, it takes them 40 minutes to get through all the checks - the air pressure, the cabin pressure, the fuel--
Checkin' the, you know, flights, the take-off, all the rest of it. Our checks for donkeys--
"Did someone close the gate?" "I think so."
That's- that's our- that's our donkey checks.

q: Karl protested that he was already treating Suzanne to the pictures. How did Steve imagine Karl got in on the cheap?
a: Dressed as a small child: "Me and my son, please!"
x: Claimed he was a film critic
f: Tickets were eight quid each. Ricky's version: Karl made Suzanne sit on his shoulders and wear a long coat.
ex: (laughing) How much was that? That was eight quid each. Did you pay for it though?
If I know you, you had a dressed up as a small child.
Or you made her sit on your shoulder as wear a long coat.

q: When the opening credits of Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon came up, what did the chatty woman in Steve's cinema say about the title?
f: Earlier she'd also asked "it's not subtitled is it?", even though it was the most famous foreign film in years.
ex: To her boyfriend, just ruining everything, a war film trailer comes on, Pearl Harbor or something, she goes “Nah, don't fancy that' just announcing this, “don't fancy that, too many war films', so then the trailer, then the opening credit…

I thought this was the most famous foreign film for years, it won Oscars, it was a huge film, everyone knew it was foreign, she goes and it went, the credit begins, it says Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, she went 'stupid name for a…

q: Steve, a genuine Ant and Dec fan, said they had the same everyman appeal as which double act?
f: Steve insisted he wasn't being ironic, and that they'll "always be PJ and Duncan to me".
ex: I'd like to, I'd like to hear your arguments for it, because I'll tell you this, and I'm not saying about this ironically, like 'oh I like a couple of kid's presenters' ironically, I think they're genuinely good.
...and you can see they have a good relationship as well.
They've got that sort of Morecambe and Wise everyman appeal.

q: Steve said someone once made him sit in their car to hear the intro of which song on their new stereo?
f: Steve: "Just sat there, I was like 'yeah'!" Ricky had said a DJ once called it the best rock intro ever.
ex: ...the intro it's got one of the best...oh no... I think Dr. Fox or Simon Bates said that about a track once.
(In DJ voice) “This has got to be the best intro of a rock song ever!” and the fact that I was saying it about The Who and he was saying it about 'Money For Nothing', is irrelevant.
Someone made me sit in their car once, with their new car stereo system, so that they could play me the beginning of 'Money For Nothing'.
Just sat there, I was like 'yeah'!

q: What did Steve suddenly ask his housemate Matt, whom he barely knew, as a wind-up?
a: "Have you got to know the good word of the Lord?"
f: Matt was "utterly petrified". Steve recommends it on long car journeys with strangers.
ex: Rick, I gotta tell you this, I was with, I've got this housemate, who I don't know that well, and I'd been living with him for about two months or something, right, and he was in the kitchen and he was washing up and I just turned to him…

q: As Karl's film pitch kept stalling, which Oscar winner did Steve say was 'coming in' for the next meeting?
f: Karl: "Do you want to hear more or?!" Steve: "I'm just conscious that Colin Firth's coming in. He's won an Oscar."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Comic Relief · 2011
ex: Do you want to hear more or?!
Yeah, I'd love to hear more please yeah.
I'm just conscious that Colin Firth's coming in. He's won an Oscar.

q: Ricky told Steve not to give his own opinions on the hate list. Who did Steve then sarcastically say he loved?
f: Moments earlier Steve had called him "a bit of a tit". Ricky followed up by calling Chris Moyles "a comedy genius".
ex: And also— this is one I'm strongly behind, Daniel Bedingfield. If you've ever heard him interviewed...
Yeah but I can't hate him.
Oh, if you've heard him interviewed he's such a knob.
He really is a bit of a tit...
Don't get involved, see the good about this is we don't get involved.

This is not— does not necessarily reflect our opinions. There are a couple of people that are cropping up that I'm right behind, but I'm not going to give that away. So don't don't give your opinion Steve cause then we're— then our hands…

q: At their agent's birthday, Steve was thirty quid up at the casino. What happened next, according to Ricky?
a: Ricky said it was his round, and the round cost more than thirty quid
x: He lost it all on one spin of roulette
He spent it all on a present for the agent
The casino refused to cash his chips
f: Steve was already down, he complained, "cause I had bought our agent a gift."
ex: Oh that was another time we went, alright. And he was up and he- he’d got a- got a win he was thirty quid up and so I said, “It’s your round then.” And the round was more than thirty quid and he couldn’t believe it. And he sat down and he…

I tell ya I was already down cause I had bought our agent a gift. He didn’t- I didn’t see him buy a round. And you know that thing when you’re buying a round of drinks for people you don’t even know so it’s like what’s the story there why…

q: Steve insisted he isn't tight with money. What did he say he wants instead?
a: Value for money at all times
x: To never pay for a round
To always split everything in half
To only buy things in the sales
f: Steve: "Every penny I've ever had has been money I've earned. So frankly I'm going to spend it wisely."
ex: Sorry I just need to defend myself for a minute. There are certain instances in life where, you see, you know you give me an attitude that I’m tight it’s not tight, it’s that-
